scenes.text: You finish a one hour meeting, and within seconds you get a neat summary, with action items for everyone. [1] So how does the AI actually do that? [2] Let's break down AI meeting notes.

Here's what happens after you hit record. [1] The meeting audio is captured, every voice in the call. [2] Speech to text turns everything into a transcript. [3] Then speaker labelling works out who said what. [4] An LLM reads the whole transcript, [5] and writes a summary, the decisions, and the action items.

That middle step has a fancy name. [1] Speaker diarization, which simply means working out who spoke when. [2] It groups voices by how they sound, [3] matches them to the names in the call, [4] and labels every line of the transcript.

data.definition: Working out who spoke when, so every line of the transcript has a name.

scenes.text: And the LLM step is really just a well written prompt. [1] A lazy prompt, like summarise this, gives you a vague paragraph. [2] Real tools send something more like this. A role, you are a meeting assistant. [3] Context, here's today's transcript, with names. [4] The task, list the decisions, and who does what, by when. [5] And the format, short bullet points. [6] And that's how you get notes that are actually useful.

data.heading: The prompt behind the notes
data.badReply: The team discussed several topics and agreed to follow up later.

List decisions and action items, with owners and dates.
data.goodReply: Decision: launch on the 15th. Priya: final designs by Friday. Rahul: budget by Tuesday.

scenes.text: So where will you find this? [1] Zoom, Google Meet and Microsoft Teams all offer AI summaries. [2] Note taker apps record in person meetings, and even lectures. [3] And some doctors use similar tools to write visit notes, while they talk to patients.

So what makes this tricky? [1] Crosstalk, when two people talk at the same time. [2] Names and jargon, like product names, or Indian names. [3] Long meetings, which may not fit in the context window, remember episode three? [4] And privacy, because everyone should know they're being recorded.

data.heading: The tough parts
terms: May not fit the context window

scenes.text: Here's a common myth. [1] People think AI meeting notes are always complete and correct. [2] They're a great first draft, but they can miss sarcasm, mix up speakers, or even invent an action item. So always skim them before you share.

data.myth: AI meeting notes are always complete and correct.
data.fact: Great first draft, but they can mix up speakers or invent an action item. Skim before sharing.
